Deluxe Pedicure Menu Details: Package, Time, and Finish

The Deluxe Pedicure at Element Nail Bar costs $49 and includes an herbal soak, sugar exfoliation, callus care, jade stones and an eight-minute massage. Check the live menu for current timing, add-ons and booking details.

By Element Nail Bar Editorial TeamSeptember 5, 2026Updated September 22, 20265 min read

In this guide

deluxe pedicure package detailsCompare services →View menu & pricing →

Short answer

A deluxe pedicure is a salon-defined service level rather than a universal package. The useful comparison is the salon’s current booking catalog: exact service name, listed price, total appointment duration, included finish, and separately bookable add-ons. The word “deluxe” alone does not establish particular products, tools, massage minutes, or treatment steps.

At Element Nail Bar on 16th Street, the active booking catalog lists the Deluxe Pedicure at $49 for 40 minutes. Regular polish is included. Optional add-ons are booked separately. The owner-confirmed Deluxe Pedicure includes an herbal soak, sugar exfoliation, callus care, jade stones, and an eight-minute massage. The active catalog also lists a $49 base price and a 40-minute appointment slot. That 40-minute slot is not a promise about total visit length when extra work is requested.

What the booking catalog confirms

The reliable starting point is the saved appointment listing. Deluxe Pedicure is one of eight base pedicure choices available in Element 16 online booking. Its listed total is 40 minutes and its price is $49. Regular polish is included, while optional add-ons have their own price and time.

That information is enough to compare the reservation without guessing at a hidden sequence. The owner has confirmed that Deluxe includes an herbal soak, sugar exfoliation, callus care, jade stones, and an eight-minute massage. The confirmation does not establish specific herbal ingredients, whether the stones are heated, an exact treatment sequence, medical effects, or sanitation procedures. Ask the salon directly about any detail that would determine whether you book.

A 40-minute base slot also should not be treated as the final duration when extra work is requested. Gel polish is listed as a separate 15-minute add-on. Callus Removal and French are also separately listed options. Tell the salon about the desired finish and any current product so the reservation can reflect the complete request.

How Deluxe differs from the other Element 16 tiers

Classic Pedicure is listed at $35 for 25 minutes, while Deluxe Pedicure is $49 for 40 minutes. Organic Spa Pedicure is a separate $65, 50-minute service. The other base choices are Pearl Spa, Róse Berry, Jelly Spa, CBD Experience, and Gold Enchantment. Together, the current catalog has eight base pedicures.

Those names, prices, and total durations are verified catalog facts. They do not establish unlisted ingredients or details beyond the confirmed eight-minute massage. A higher price or longer duration may help a guest narrow the list, but anyone choosing by a particular product or step should confirm it directly with the salon.

You do not need to memorize the lineup. The Element 16 pedicure comparison presents the current base choices. Use the exact booking names so the reservation is attached to the intended service rather than a generic use of “deluxe” or “spa.”

Who gets the most value from Deluxe

Deluxe is a sensible choice when all three of these statements are true:

  1. You want the specific Deluxe Pedicure listing rather than the shorter Classic reservation.
  2. A $49 base price and 40-minute listed duration fit the visit you are planning.
  3. You have checked whether your requested finish or add-on needs extra time.

Classic may fit when its $35 price and 25-minute duration better match the plan. Organic Spa or another longer base pedicure may fit when you want to reserve a longer catalog slot. The booking catalog supports that time-and-price comparison; it does not explain every product or step behind each name.

Deluxe is not selected by gender, age, or polish color. It is selected as a named base service. Someone who wants no color can ask whether Shinny Buff or another finish is appropriate and how it should be booked. Detailed toenail art, repairs, or other additions may require a separate selection and more time. If two guests want appointments together, mention that before choosing a time. The service name establishes the base reservation, while the booking note gives the salon the practical details needed to confirm availability and duration.

What the $49 price does and does not cover

The posted $49 figure is the current base price for the Deluxe Pedicure. It does not make every possible appointment $49. Element’s booking catalog lists Gel Polish at $15 for 15 minutes, French at $15 for 15 minutes, and Callus Removal at $10 for 15 minutes. Other pedicure add-ons are listed separately as well. Describe the requested result and let the salon confirm which additions belong on the reservation.

Existing product can also affect the scope. If you arrive with gel polish or an enhancement on a toenail, removal may need to be booked. A damaged enhancement or a requested acrylic toenail is different from standard polish work. Sending that information in advance gives the team a chance to reserve the proper category.

Review the live menu before relying on any number in a future-dated article. Prices, timing, and service descriptions can change. The current menu and a direct salon confirmation always outrank a saved guide.

Preparing for the appointment

There is no need to trim your toenails or aggressively file rough skin before a professional pedicure. Leave enough information for the technician to see the actual starting point. Bring a polish reference if you have one, and identify the part that matters: exact color family, finish, French placement, or simple art.

Tell the salon about ingredient sensitivities before service. Pain, broken skin, or a suspected infection is not a reason to ask for stronger exfoliation. It is a reason to pause cosmetic work and consult an appropriate medical professional.

Phoenix guests often schedule pedicures around sandal-heavy weeks, pool time, weddings, or travel. Those plans can influence polish choice and appointment timing. They do not change the Deluxe service definition. If regular polish is selected, bring footwear that will not press against a fresh finish.

How to reserve Deluxe without ambiguity

Element Nail Bar is located at 6022 N 16th St, Phoenix, AZ 85016. Current hours are Monday through Saturday, 9:30 AM to 7:00 PM, and Sunday, 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Call 602-607-5686 if you need help comparing tiers or arranging side-by-side appointments.

When you are ready, book the Element 16 Deluxe Pedicure and include removal, gel, French tips, repairs, or toenail enhancements in the note. A well-scoped reservation protects the time for the service you actually want. The named service provides the starting point; the details make the appointment accurate.
